intended_object: For a TM1 machine `M : Λ → Stmt Γ Λ σ`, a finite set `S` of labels "supports" `M` when it contains the start label and is closed under the `goto` jumps made by the statements `M q` for `q ∈ S`. In other words, the part of the machine reachable from the start state is finite. This comes from the docstring and from its use in `step_supports` and `stmts_supportsStmt`.
explanation:
The body has two conditions: `default ∈ S`, and `SupportsStmt S (M q)` for every `q ∈ S`. `SupportsStmt` goes recursively through move/write/load/branch. It requires every possible target `l a v` of a `goto` to lie in `S`, and puts no condition on `halt`. This is exactly the closure condition in the docstring.

The docstring does not mention the requirement that the start label `default` be in `S`. That requirement is still the intended one: the analogous `TM0.Supports` also has it, and it is what lets `step_supports` show that every reachable configuration stays inside `S`. So the omission is not a mismatch.

Using `Finset` instead of `Set` is deliberate. The point of the notion is to show that the machine has finitely many reachable states (`stmts` is a `Finset` built from `S`), so this is not a loss of generality.

Mathlib has no more general version of this notion. It is the TM1 analogue of `Turing.TM0.Supports`, not a special case of it. The definition is faithful.
